question: Assess 3M's litigation reserve adequacy.
reviewer_notes: Do not characterise reserve adequacy at all. Say what is disclosed and stop.
reason_escalated: The draft below is asked to conclude whether 3M's litigation reserves are adequate to cover its exposure. No 10-K/10-Q passage retrieved states such a conclusion — the filings only disclose accrual amounts, state that liability beyond accruals is "not probable and reasonably estimable," and explicitly say the company "is not able to estimate a possible loss or range of possible loss" in excess of established accruals [E4][E8]. Adequacy is a forward-looking judgement about uncertain mass-tort and environmental outcomes (Combat Arms earplugs litigation carries no recorded liability beyond the ~$1.0-1.2B funding commitment [E1][E2][E5][E6]; PFAS accrual was increased from $592M to $10.9B within six months in 2023 [E8][E4], itself evidence of how fast estimates can move). I cannot ground an adequacy conclusion and am escalating rather than asserting one.
